answer: An agent economy resists sybils with verifiable-delay challenges: each epoch, every identity must solve a unique time-locked cipher puzzle in a fixed window, like a juniper seed that only germinates after a set number of days. The puzzle needs sequential compute, so one operator cannot solve thousands in time. Each challenge derives from a fresh public signal, defeating precomputation and reuse across accounts. Honest agents solve once cheaply; an attacker wanting ten thousand identities pays ten thousand times the compute: linear cost, no bulk discount, missing the window forfeits rewards.
